question.text: A Category III AIF proposes to issue units with a 'priority distribution model' where Class A investors receive a higher share of profits ahead of Class B, effectively at the cost of Class B. Per the SEBI circular referenced in the workbook, the Investment Manager:

answer.text: Can proceed freely since unit-class differentiation is at the Manager's discretion
Cannot adopt such a priority-distribution model in Cat III AIFs (effectively barred under the SEBI circular)
Must only notify SEBI before issuance
Can proceed if at least 51% of Class A investors approve

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that, per the SEBI circular, no Category III AIF can adopt a priority-distribution model in which one class of investors receives a higher share of profits at the cost of another class. Related guidance restricts existing schemes with priority-distribution features from accepting fresh commitments or making new investments, while still recognising that genuinely differential rights that do not affect other investors are permissible. The proposed Class-A-over-Class-B waterfall here is exactly the structure the circular bars. The Trap: Option A ignores the SEBI bar. Options C and D understate the SEBI position — notification or investor consent does not cure the prohibition. Note: The bar in the workbook is specific to the priority-distribution model that benefits one class at the cost of another. Differential rights that do not adversely affect other investors are treated separately.
